key_insight: Prompts can systematically override the visual input in large vision-language models, causing hallucinations; HalluScope quantifies this prompt-induced failure mode and isolates when language instructions dominate vision.
problem_solved: Clarifies and measures a previously ambiguous source of hallucinations in LVLMs by separating prompt-driven effects from vision-backbone and language-dominance factors.
method: Introduce HalluScope: a benchmark of curated image + prompt pairs designed to elicit and measure prompt-induced hallucinations.
Systematically vary prompt templates and instruction content to probe when and how prompts cause outputs that contradict the visual evidence.
Evaluate multiple LVLMs using automated metrics and human judgments to quantify hallucination rates and attribute failures to prompt vs. visual components.
impact: Provides practitioners a diagnostic tool and empirical evidence to detect, measure, and mitigate prompt-induced errors in multimodal systems, informing safer prompt engineering and model design.
visual_elements: Flow diagram showing interaction between image encoder, prompt text, and LLM decoder with an overlay indicating 'prompt override' pathways.
Bar chart comparing hallucination rates across models and prompt types (neutral vs. leading prompts).
Side-by-side example panels: image + benign prompt → grounded answer, image + leading prompt → hallucinated answer.
Heatmap or sensitivity plot showing how small prompt changes increase hallucination probability.
paper_title: When Prompts Override Vision: Prompt-Induced Hallucinations in LVLMs
paper_authors: Pegah Khayatan, Jayneel Parekh, Arnaud Dapogny, Mustafa Shukor, Alasdair Newson
